_about: Principles shown in the principle drawer (Ctrl+Space). Edit this file, then press Refresh in the drawer.
Keys starting with an underscore are ignored, use them for notes like this one.
Required: title (unique), spotElo (whole number 0-4000), description, gamePart, focus.
Optional: explanation (Markdown, one text or a list of lines), image (path relative to this file), enabled (true/false, default true).
gamePart: opening, midgame, attacking midgame, defending midgame, endgame
focus: pawn, knight, bishop, rook, queen, king, space, strategy, coordination
The difficulty tag follows from spotElo: up to 600 beginner, up to 1200 intermediate, up to 1800 advanced, above that expert.
enabled only counts the first time a title shows up, after that the drawer keeps your choice. Renaming a title makes it a new principle.
Whether the engine can actually use a principle is decided by the engine, not by this file.
The four principles below are examples of the layout, replace them with your own.

principles.title: Develop your pieces
principles.description: Bring knights and bishops off the back rank before moving any piece twice.
explanation: Every tempo in the opening counts. A piece that is still on its starting square takes no part in the fight.
- Early queen adventures that lose time
- Moving the same piece several times

principles.title: Rooks belong on open files
principles.description: Place rooks on files without pawns so they can reach the seventh rank.

principles.title: Knight outposts
principles.description: A knight on a square no enemy pawn can attack, supported by its own pawn, is very strong.
principles.explanation: Outposts usually appear on holes in the opponent's pawn structure, often on the fifth or sixth rank.

principles.title: Prophylaxis
principles.description: Ask what the opponent wants to do and stop it before improving your own position.
